story_type: in-flight launch abort test, rocket breaks apart
hook: SpaceX let this rocket break apart with a crew capsule on top.
narration: This Falcon 9 broke apart over Florida, and SpaceX planned it that way.
On January nineteenth, twenty twenty, it lifted off from Launch Complex 39A at Kennedy Space Center with a Crew Dragon on top.
The job was to prove Crew Dragon could get away from a rocket that fails during launch.
A launch escape works like an ejection seat for the whole capsule. Engines built into its sides fire and push it clear in seconds.
About a minute and a half after liftoff, the capsule triggered its escape. [short pause]
It fired away, and the rocket it left behind came apart in the sky.
Then a camera on the capsule watched its parachutes open.
outcome: Crew Dragon splashed down just off the Florida coast, and every major step of the escape worked.
title: Rocket broke apart, capsule escaped
description:
On Jan. 19, 2020, SpaceX and NASA flew an in-flight abort test from Kennedy Space Center: Crew Dragon escaped its Falcon 9, which broke apart as planned, and splashed down off Florida.

facts.claim: Test on Jan. 19, 2020 from Launch Complex 39A to show Crew Dragon can separate from a failing Falcon 9
facts.source_quote: NASA and SpaceX conduct an In-Flight Abort Test on Jan. 19, 2020, to demonstrate Crew Dragon's ability to safely separate from a Falcon 9 rocket in the unlikely event of a failure during launch. Liftoff occurred at 10:30 a.m. EST from Launch Complex 39A at the agency's Kennedy Space Center in Florida.

facts.claim: Escape triggered about 1.5 minutes after liftoff
facts.source_quote: SpaceX configured Crew Dragon to trigger a launch escape about 1.5 minutes after liftoff.
begin the recovery effort of the Falcon 9, which broke apart as planned.

facts.claim: Splashdown off the Florida coast; all major functions worked
facts.source_quote: Crew Dragon splashed down at 10:38 a.m. just off the Florida coast in the Atlantic Ocean.
All major functions were executed, including separation, engine firings, parachute deployment and landing.
